questions.q: Which compound CANNOT undergo self aldol condensation with dilute NaOH?
questions.explain: (CH₃)₃C–CHO has no α-hydrogen, so no enolate can form; like HCHO and C₆H₅CHO it gives the Cannizzaro reaction in concentrated alkali instead.

questions.q: Propanal is treated with cold dilute NaOH. The aldol formed is:
questions.explain: The α-carbon (C-2) of one propanal bonds to the carbonyl carbon of the other, so the methyl branch sits at C-2 and the OH at C-3. Joining through C-3 (giving 3-hydroxyhexanal) is the common trap.

questions.q: Heptane-2,6-dione is warmed with aqueous OH⁻. The major product is:
questions.explain: This 1,5-diketone cyclises by an intramolecular aldol: the C-1 enolate attacks the C-6 carbonyl, and dehydration gives the strain-free six-membered enone. Because every step is reversible, the four-membered ring does not accumulate.

questions.q: In vinylogous self-condensation, CH₃(CH=CH)ₙCHO with n = 100 reacts with a second identical molecule in base on heating. The value of n in the product CH₃(CH=CH)ₙCHO is:
questions.explain: The acidic γ-CH₃ of one molecule attacks the CHO of the other and water is lost, so self-condensation gives CH₃(CH=CH)₂ₙ₊₁CHO: 2(100) + 1 = 201.
